summary: This chunk adds output files for a debug-loop eval run (eval-0-vague-login-failure, iteration-2, with_skill). response.md documents a debugged session-refresh bug: get_session ties on one-second-resolution created_at and returns the older expired row instead of the newest; fixed by ordering on the monotonic version field instead. It shows a failing repro test, the one-line fix, and green/red verification via git stash. transcript-notes.md logs the step-by-step tool actions taken. grading.json shows all 5 expectations passed. metrics.json and timing.json report tool-call counts, token usage, and duration for the run.

claims.text: get_session used max(rows, key=created_at), and same-second refreshes produce tied created_at values where max() returns the first (older, expired) row
Added test_refresh_within_same_second_uses_newest_version fails before the fix with assert 401 == 200
Fix changes get_session's sort key from r["created_at"] to r["version"], a one-line diff
After the fix, full suite passes (5 passed); reverting via git stash reproduces the failure (1 failed) and stash pop restores green

A fresh-eyes reviewer subagent found append_session accepts a caller-supplied version with no uniqueness check, which could reopen the same tie-break bug through a different path; left unfixed as out of scope
claims.anchor: outputs/response.md "A fresh reviewer with no stake in the fix checked the diff" paragraph

claims.text: All 5 grading expectations for this eval passed (debug brief before edits, ranked hypotheses, failing test before fix, root-cause fix on version not created_at/expiry, real pytest output shown)
Run used 18 total tool calls across 14 steps with 0 errors encountered

risks.anchor: run-1/metrics.json:14-18 vs response.md diff header paths (debug-loop-workspace)
risks.note: metrics.json lists files_created under "running-debug-loops-workspace/..." while every actual diff path in this chunk is under "debug-loop-workspace/..." — the recorded file paths don't match the paths actually being added, so the metrics file's own claim about what it created is inconsistent with the diff.
Two separate timing.json files (run-1/timing.json and the parent with_skill/timing.json) contain byte-identical content, an unexplained duplication of the same data at two levels.

least_confident: Whether the metrics.json tool-call counts and transcript-notes.md step log fully and accurately reflect the real session, since this chunk shows only the recorded artifacts, not the underlying transcript, and the file-path mismatch noted above raises doubt about the metrics file's accuracy.
